issues.legal_issue: A statutory prohibition on subletting overrides a lease term that permits subletting.
material_facts: The lease letter expressly permitted the tenant to keep sub-tenants in the new premises.
The tenant sublet part of the premises after the statutory prohibition had come into operation.
The landlord sought ejectment on the ground of the subletting.
issues.conclusion: The statutory prohibition applied to contracts as well as other laws, so the lease term permitting subletting was unenforceable.
issues.legal_principle: Section 15 of the Bombay Hotel and Lodging Houses Rates Control Act, 1947, made subletting unlawful notwithstanding anything contained in any law; contracts fall within the law relating to contracts. Under section 23 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, an agreement contrary to that prohibition is unenforceable. Section 13(1)(e) is expressly subject to section 15. The Court distinguished section 10 of the Bombay Rents, Hotel Rates and Lodging Houses Rates (Control) Act, 1944, which permitted subletting on conditions, and Cooper v. Shiavax Cambatta, which concerned that different statutory scheme.

predicates.landlord_tenant_subletting_dispute: A dispute between a landlord and tenant concerns the tenant's subletting of leased premises.
predicates.lease_terms_permit_subletting: The lease terms state that the tenant may sublet the premises.
predicates.tenant_sublet_after_prohibition: The tenant sublets the premises after a statutory prohibition on subletting has taken effect.

issues.definition: When a landlord-tenant subletting dispute involves lease permission and subletting after a statutory prohibition takes effect, the private permission cannot authorize that subletting.

issues.legal_issue: A landlord who participated in an arrangement permitting subletting may still seek the statutory remedy for the tenant's prohibited subletting.
material_facts: The landlord's lease letter recognized and permitted subletting.
The tenant sublet the premises in breach of the statutory prohibition.
The landlord sought ejectment under the statutory remedy, not enforcement of the lease term concerning subletting.
issues.conclusion: The landlord could seek ejectment under the statute despite having permitted the subletting, because the claim enforced a statutory right rather than the illegal agreement.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 15 and 13(1)(e) of the Bombay Hotel and Lodging Houses Rates Control Act, 1947, respectively prohibit subletting and provide for recovery of possession on that ground. The in pari delicto principle does not prevent a court from granting a remedy grounded directly in a statute when the claimant is not asking the court to enforce the illegal agreement. The Court relied on Bowmakers Ltd. v. Barnet Instruments Ltd. and Gibbs & Sterret Manufacturing Co. v. Brucker, and observed that public policy may permit relief by way of restitution or rescission even to an equal participant in illegality, though not on the contract.

predicates.landlord_tenant_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brings an eviction proceeding against a tenant.
predicates.tenant_sublet_prohibited_premises: The tenant sublets premises in circumstances where the subletting is prohibited.
predicates.landlord_seeks_statutory_remedy_not_cont: The landlord seeks a remedy created by statute rather than asking the court to enforce the agreement permitting the subletting.

issues.definition: In an eviction proceeding, when the tenant has made a prohibited subletting and the landlord seeks a statutory remedy rather than enforcement of the agreement, the landlord may obtain the statutory ejectment remedy.

issues.legal_issue: A landlord cannot waive a statutory prohibition on subletting where enforcing the waiver would give effect to the prohibited agreement.
material_facts: The landlord expressly permitted the tenant to keep sub-tenants in the premises.
The tenant relied on that permission to argue that the landlord had waived the right to seek ejectment.
The prohibition was treated by the Court as based on public policy, and ejectment was sought under the statute.
issues.conclusion: The waiver plea could not defeat ejectment because giving effect to it would enforce an illegal agreement and contravene the statutory prohibition.
issues.legal_principle: A waiver of a right may ordinarily be inferred from conduct, but an agreement to waive an illegality is void on grounds of public policy. A statutory prohibition inserted in the public interest cannot be neutralized by consent, acquiescence, failure to plead, or waiver. The Court relied on Surajmull Nargoremull v. Triton Insurance Co., Nixon v. Albion Marine Insurance Co., Dhanukudhari Singh v. Nathima Sahu, Bowmakers Ltd. v. Barnet Instruments Ltd., and the authorities quoted in the judgment concerning waiver of illegality. It also noted that waiver is a mixed question of law and fact and had not been raised below, but rejected the plea on its merits even assuming it could be considered.

rule.if: landlord_tenant_eviction_proceeding and lease_terms_permit_subletting and tenant_sublet_prohibited_premises and landlord_invokes_waiver

predicates.landlord_tenant_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brings an eviction proceeding against a tenant.
predicates.lease_terms_permit_subletting: The lease terms state that the tenant may sublet the premises.
predicates.tenant_sublet_prohibited_premises: The tenant sublets premises in circumstances where the subletting is prohibited.
predicates.landlord_invokes_waiver: The tenant relies on the landlord's permission or conduct as a waiver of the right to seek eviction.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks eviction over prohibited subletting, the tenant cannot use the landlord's permission or conduct as a waiver to bar the statutory remedy.
